It was read at the pinned revision below to write a behaviour specification. Ravel's counterpart is an independent implementation and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or derived from the original's source text.

publication.notes: The fetched source lives only in the public repository's ignored fixture tree at tests/fixtures/local/m6-clean-room/ and is not tracked. The specification derived from it is tracked at specifications/m6-foundation/RVL-321.md and is published in-tree in this public repository. The upstream material is not cleared for publication while the names surface is unresolved. The fetched tree includes the entry's binary assets (773 texture files) and its declarative model and data files; the textures were not read as behaviour and nothing is shipped from them.
publication.reviewedBy: structure-reviewed 2026-09-05 by an independent Claude reader that had seen no upstream source; it read the specification first and then the counterpart's module list and public types to see whether a structural noun had crossed, after the counterpart was implemented; verdict: accepted; the specification's read/inferred/unknown markers and closing coverage statement were checked present. No human has read the specification in full.

rights.basis: MIT, read at the source rather than trusted from the inventory. Reading, modification and derivative works are permitted, which is what source-informed reimplementation requires. The counterpart must not copy source text; the specification written from this read carries no upstream identifier, which checks/verify-spec-identifiers.sh was run over and returned no finding.
MIT imposes no behavioural restriction and the inventory records behaviour as cleared and sourceUse as permitted for this entry.

Unchanged from the inventory. MIT does not grant trademark rights, so the project's own name, its mod id and its content identifiers remain unresolved. The specification therefore names nothing after the original, and no save-compatible identifier mapping is specified.

773 texture files were fetched with the source and not read. The inventory records textures as cleared for this artifact and the licence reserves no asset separately. Nothing upstream is tracked or shipped; any counterpart art is rewritten from reference under policies/source-access.json and recorded in the package's assets-provenance.json.

The fetched tree carries no binary model file; its models are declarative model documents fetched with the source and read only for the registration census the specification records. The inventory records models as cleared for this artifact and the licence reserves no asset separately. Nothing upstream is tracked or shipped.

The fetched tree contains no sound file, which is what the inventory's not-applicable verdict for this artifact holds. The specification's sound references name host sounds rather than any shipped with the entry.
No branding material was fetched or read; the display name, logo and author identity are excluded regardless of licence status under policies/source-access.json.
